name: Ztech
tagline: Waste-to-Wonder parks + industrial-wastewater EPC pivoting to a recurring annuity model (Zing Parks) -- strong FY26 growth, but cash-conversion quality is the open question
verdict_headline: Genuine circular-economy/smart-city niche with a credible annuity pivot, but working-capital quality and a mid-year CFO exit cap conviction at Medium until FY27 guidance starts converting to cash
verdict_reasoning: four_box score 3.0 (tailwind yes, tam yes, moat weak, valuation weak) permits a 10x-in-2-3-years call, not the earlier 100x-in-10-years light-pass label -- moat is unproven and the FY27 guidance has zero guided-vs-delivered track record yet
FY26 revenue +65% YoY to Rs155.8cr, PAT +83% to Rs35.86cr, nil promoter pledge confirmed for FY26 -- real operating momentum

But FY26 trade receivables nearly doubled (Rs48.9cr -> Rs94.0cr), screener shows historically negative operating cash flow, and management's own explanation (parks commissioned ahead of collecting EPC payments) is exactly the pattern that precedes a cash-flow scare -- needs 2-3 quarters of clean collection before trusting the P&L growth

CFO resignation (May 2026) mid-scale-up plus conflicting debt disclosures across sources (almost-debt-free claims vs Rs75cr reported borrowings) are governance/data-quality flags, not yet red-flag-tier, but real

Conviction held at Medium (not Medium-High) pending resolution of the cash-conversion and debt-disclosure questions; red_flag_tier stays CLEAR -- no auditor resignation or going-concern signal, and nil pledge is a genuine mitigant
business_overview: Z-Tech (India) Ltd operates three verticals: (1) sustainable 'Waste-to-Wonder' theme parks built from recycled municipal waste under government mandates (Delhi, Ayodhya, Bihar, and the flagship Krishna-Lok park in UP), now scaling into a recurring-revenue platform branded Zing Parks (ticketing, retail, F&B, events, adventure activities); (2) industrial wastewater management using proprietary GEIST technology (500M+ gallons recycled); (3) geotechnical/mining-stabilisation engineering services. The company is explicitly repositioning from a pure EPC/construction contractor toward what management calls an 'integrated sustainability-led infrastructure company', with annuity revenue from operating parks targeted to scale from Rs8cr (FY26) to Rs40-42cr (FY27).

fundamentals_narrative: Z-Tech's P&L has genuinely inflected -- FY26 revenue growth re-accelerated to 65% after decelerating from FY24's high base, PAT grew faster than revenue on improving mix, and the company is executing a credible multi-year pivot from lumpy government EPC contracts toward a recurring annuity model (Zing Parks) that should improve earnings quality over time if it scales as guided (annuity revenue 5x from Rs8cr to Rs40-42cr in FY27 alone). The balance-sheet picture is murkier: receivables nearly doubled in FY26 against 65% revenue growth, working-capital days have been elongating by multiple independent readings (though sources disagree on the exact magnitude), and screener's FY25 cash-flow data shows a sharply negative operating cash flow -- management's own explanation is that parks were commissioned (and revenue booked) ahead of collecting the underlying EPC payments, which is a textbook aggressive-recognition pattern worth watching closely rather than dismissing. Debt figures conflict across sources (near-zero vs ~Rs75cr), which itself is a data-quality flag pending a direct annual-report read. No promoter pledge and a declining-but-not-collapsing promoter stake (~60.75% to ~52% over roughly two years, partly attributable to the SME-to-mainboard listing dilution) round out the picture: real business momentum, real execution record on winning and delivering marquee government contracts (Krishna-Lok, Ayodhya being the largest to date), but the cash-conversion and disclosure-consistency questions need another 2-3 quarters to resolve before the growth can be trusted at face value.
bse_notes: NSE filing (23 Mar 2026): business update on 'Saat Ajoobe Park' / Krishna-Lok Waste-to-Wonder park win, UP's largest such order to date (~Rs19cr+, 34 acres, 20-year revenue-sharing structure, Z-Tech's own upfront investment only ~Rs1.9cr). CFO change: Vikas Jain resigned effective 29 May 2026, Isha Chaudhary appointed. Promoter pledge confirmation (2 Apr 2026): nil pledge for FY26. Auditor: NAV & Co, no resignation found.
bull_case: Pioneering a national-scale 'Waste-to-Wonder' niche riding India's circular-economy and Smart Cities push, with very few organised listed competitors in the exact combination of parks + industrial wastewater (GEIST) + geotechnical services

Explicit, funded pivot from lumpy EPC revenue to recurring Zing Parks annuity income (ticketing/F&B/events) -- annuity revenue guided to grow 5x (Rs8cr -> Rs40-42cr) in FY27 alone, which would materially improve earnings quality and revenue visibility if delivered
FY26 delivered real operating momentum: revenue +65%, PAT +83%, EBITDA +55%, and the company scaled from 4 to 11 operational parks with a 15-park FY27 target
Nil promoter pledge, and the single largest order to date (Krishna-Lok, Ayodhya) demonstrates the company can win and execute marquee state-government mandates

Stock has corrected roughly a third from 2026 highs (~Rs595 -> ~Rs400) even as FY26 earnings grew sharply, which has brought the trailing multiple down from ~32x to roughly high-teens, improving the entry point versus the growth on offer if the cash-conversion concerns prove transitory
bear_case: Working-capital/cash-conversion quality is the central risk: trade receivables nearly doubled (Rs49cr -> Rs94cr) against 65% revenue growth in FY26, and screener's FY25 data shows a sharply negative operating cash flow (~ -Rs91cr) -- management's own explanation (parks commissioned ahead of collecting EPC payments) is the kind of pattern that has preceded real cash-flow problems at other small-cap EPC-adjacent names

CFO resignation mid-FY26 just as the business scales into a more complex multi-segment, multi-revenue-stream model is a governance/bench-strength flag worth monitoring, even without any other red-flag trigger

Materially conflicting disclosures on debt levels across sources (near-debt-free claims vs a reported ~Rs75cr in borrowings) -- this needs to be resolved against the actual FY26 annual report before the balance sheet can be trusted at face value

Moat is weak: park construction/EPC work is replicable by other infrastructure contractors, and the GEIST wastewater technology's differentiation is unproven at scale against larger water-treatment players

FY27 guidance (Rs250-260cr revenue, 15 parks, 50 lakh footfall, Rs40-42cr annuity revenue, Rs5-10cr debt reduction) is the company's first real multi-year guidance -- there is no guided-vs-delivered track record yet, and the company itself flags political/approval-timeline delay risk on municipal park commissioning

Zero dividend despite consistent profitability, and a declining promoter stake (~60.75% to ~52% over roughly two years) -- individually explainable (SME-to-mainboard dilution, reinvestment phase) but worth tracking alongside the other flags

deep_dive.conviction_update: Low-Medium -> Medium. FY26 operating momentum (+65% revenue, +83% PAT) and a credible, funded pivot toward a recurring annuity model justify moving off the light-pass floor, but the receivables/cash-flow build, conflicting debt disclosures, and a mid-year CFO exit are real enough to withhold Medium-High until the next 1-2 quarters show the cash conversion normalising.

earnings_chain.bottleneck_link: park commissioning and footfall ramp, constrained by political/municipal approval timelines (flagged by the company itself)
earnings_chain.operating_leverage: unclear -- management guides a margin-mix benefit as annuity revenue scales, but FY26 EBITDA margin actually contracted ~186bps YoY despite the annuity share of revenue growing, so the guided operating leverage has not yet shown up in the reported numbers

market_expectation.implied_growth_cagr: Directionally, roughly 15-20% EPS CAGR FY26-28 would justify today's ~17x at a cautious 18-20x exit multiple appropriate for a small-cap with unresolved cash-conversion questions; FY26 already delivered 83% PAT growth, so the bar is on sustaining collection quality, not on topline growth
market_expectation.our_fy27_estimate: Revenue roughly in line with the Rs250-260cr guidance (+60-67%); margin likely flat to modestly better as annuity mix rises, partly offset by continued EPC execution drag; PAT growth likely trails revenue growth if receivables keep building faster than collections
market_expectation.our_fy28_estimate: A genuine second leg is plausible from the annuity base (Rs40-42cr -> higher) and a 15+ park footprint, but this is contingent on working-capital/cash-conversion normalising first -- not yet evidenced
market_expectation.gap_basis: The stock has corrected roughly a third from 2026 highs even as FY26 earnings grew sharply, so the market has already given back some of the prior re-rating; what remains unpriced either way is the resolution of the cash-conversion/receivables question, which could re-rate the stock further (if it resolves cleanly) or compress the multiple further (if it doesn't)
market_expectation.data_caveat: no broker consensus; implied path is a reverse-P/E estimate + screener.in forward figures + VP thread view

catalyst.event: FY27 results showing execution against the Rs250-260cr revenue / 15-park / 50-lakh-footfall / Rs40-42cr annuity-revenue guidance, alongside evidence that receivables are actually converting to cash

value_chain.theme: circular-economy / waste-to-wonder municipal infrastructure, industrial wastewater treatment, and geotechnical engineering
value_chain.position: EPC contractor and build-operate theme-park developer for state/municipal waste-to-wonder mandates, migrating toward an annuity/recurring-revenue operating model (Zing Parks) alongside proprietary GEIST industrial-wastewater technology and geotechnical/mining-stabilisation services
value_chain.bottleneck_node: municipal/state government approval and commissioning timelines -- explicitly flagged by the company as a risk to its own guidance
value_chain.note: No direct listed peer replicates the exact combination of waste-to-wonder parks + industrial wastewater + geotechnical services; the closest comparables sit in the broader water/wastewater-treatment EPC space. The waste-to-wonder park format remains a government-mandate niche Z-Tech effectively pioneered, with limited organised competition so far -- a soft, relationship-based moat rather than a structural one.

drivers: working-capital-driven cash-margin drag from the receivables build
earnings_quality.normalised_note: FY26 EBITDA margin (27.6%) actually contracted ~186bps YoY despite revenue scaling 65% and the annuity mix growing, so the business is not currently printing a cyclically elevated margin -- if anything, near-term margin is depressed by the EPC-heavy recognition pattern and working-capital drag rather than inflated by one-offs.

growth_trajectory.last_quarters_note: Annual revenue: Rs26cr (FY23) -> Rs67cr (FY24, +158%) -> Rs94.4cr (FY25, +40%) -> Rs155.8cr (FY26, +65%) -- a genuinely non-monotonic, order-driven growth pattern typical of a government-EPC-linked business; within FY26 itself, one source (whalesbook) flags cooling sequential quarterly momentum even as the YoY comparison stayed strong
growth_trajectory.reverse_pe_note: Even after the ~33% price correction from 2026 highs, the current multiple needs continued high-teens-to-20%+ EPS growth to hold; FY26 cleared that bar comfortably on a reported basis (83% PAT growth), but the real test is whether that growth converts to cash rather than receivables

management_quality.capital_allocation: Reinvesting operating cash flow plus some fresh borrowing into park construction and mining-stabilisation equipment; incremental ROCE is difficult to isolate cleanly given the working-capital swings and conflicting debt disclosures; no unrelated-diversification red flag noted
management_quality.capability_ladder_note: Explicit, stated transition from pure EPC contractor to an 'integrated sustainability-led infrastructure company' via the Zing Parks recurring-revenue platform -- a genuine value-chain-upgrade narrative, though unproven at scale

track_record.note: FY24 (157.7% revenue growth, 61% ROCE), FY25 (40.3% revenue growth, 28% ROCE), and FY26 (65.9% revenue growth, 20% ROCE) met the dual threshold (revenue growth ≥10% AND ROCE ≥15%). Light-lane P&L + Ratios review: Mar 2021–2026 screener.in standalone series (oldest data available).

four_box.note: Tailwind and TAM remain genuinely strong (national circular-economy/smart-city push, only 11 of a potentially much larger addressable set of municipalities served so far). Moat stays weak (replicable EPC work, unproven GEIST differentiation at scale). Valuation stays weak -- despite a ~33% price correction improving the entry multiple, the unresolved receivables/cash-conversion and debt-disclosure questions mean the lower multiple may be appropriately discounting real risk rather than offering a clean bargain.

shareholding_pattern.note: Promoter holding declined from ~60.75% (mid-2024) to ~52% (latest) -- a meaningful multi-quarter downtrend, plausibly amplified by the company's SME-to-mainboard listing/fundraise dilution rather than pure promoter selling. Formally confirmed nil pledge for FY26 (2 Apr 2026 NSE filing), so this is NOT a concurrent pledge-rising/holding-falling red flag -- but the declining stake is worth continuing to watch.
